name: DevMPNN-Bench
description: Evaluation resource for developability-oriented inverse folding. Contains 35 monomeric PDB backbones (chain A, 56-415 residues, 30 X-ray and 5 NMR), 11 design arms (ProteinMPNN, SolubleMPNN, HyperMPNN, MembraneMPNN global-label, LigandMPNN, and five closed-form guidance arms), 5,936 designs at 16 designs per arm-backbone cell, per-design physicochemical properties with native recovery and diversity, ESMFold-v1 refold scTM for every design, Protenix-2 single-sequence scTM for a robustness subset, and aggregates with paired bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm-corrected p-values. The resource is intended for evaluating what developability control costs in foldability, how much unrequested properties leak, and how arm-level means hide per-backbone failure modes.
citeAs: Anonymous Authors. DevMPNN-Bench: What Developability Benchmarks Do Not Measure. NeurIPS 2027 Evaluations & Datasets track submission (under review).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Folded outputs were deduplicated keeping the last row per (arm, backbone, design) identifier; no rows were filtered by value. One documented alignment artefact (backbone 1TEN, 90 vs 89 CA) is retained and disclosed in the paper Limitations, with an exclusion sensitivity analysis.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Properties are computed from designed sequences: net charge at pH 7.4 from a standard pKa table, isoelectric point by bisection, GRAVY from the Kyte-Doolittle scale, aggregation propensity as the fraction of exposed 5-residue windows with >=3 apolar residues, and surface apolar fraction as the apolar fraction over the less-buried half of residues (CA burial proxy, validated against Shrake-Rupley SASA on six backbones).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are computational, not human annotations. Native recovery is the per-design identity to the PDB chain-A sequence. scTM is TM-score of the ESMFold-v1 refolded design against the input backbone (chain A, three recycles). The second-oracle scTM uses Protenix-2 in single-sequence mode. Physicochemical labels are computed from sequence with the definitions in Appendix A of the paper. No human annotators, annotator demographics or annotation platform are involved.
rai:dataBiases: The 35 backbones are all monomeric, soluble and experimental; 19 of 35 are under 100 residues and 5 are NMR entries. Absolute scTM values are therefore optimistic for the 150-300 residue regime that dominates real design campaigns. Property proxies are coarse: surface apolarity is a burial proxy, not SASA, and aggregation is a heuristic window count with no experimental calibration.
rai:dataLimitations: Single scenario (soluble monomers); 19 of 35 backbones are under 100 residues, so absolute scTM values are optimistic for the 150-300 residue regime. One sampling temperature (T=0.1) for the main table. Only composition-linear objectives are covered. No wet-lab validation. All designed sequences and refolded structures are synthetic model outputs, not experimental measurements, and must not be interpreted as validated proteins. Five NMR structures contribute low-scTM cells for every arm.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The resource is an evaluation artifact for protein design; it does not itself produce functional proteins. Dual-use risk is the usual one for protein design tooling and is not increased by this benchmark, which measures failure modes rather than optimising designs. Compute cost: about 20 A6000 GPU-hours for the full sweep plus a few CPU-hours of sampling.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking controllability and leakage of developability-oriented inverse-folding methods
Auditing evaluation practice: saturation, arm-mean aggregation, and oracle dependence
Reproducing paired, Holm-corrected arm comparisons with an explicit minimum detectable effect
Studying per-backbone tail behaviour of design models
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Released with the paper under MIT (code) and CC BY 4.0 (text and figures). The per-design matrix and aggregates are versioned in the repository; backbones are identified by RCSB PDB accession so they can be re-fetched. No further maintenance is planned beyond fixing reported errors; corrections will be listed in a CHANGELOG.

field.name: target
field.description: RCSB PDB accession of the input backbone.

rai:dataCollectionRawData: Input backbones are public-domain experimental structures from the RCSB Protein Data Bank, identified by accession in Table B.1 and data/targets30.txt. Model weights come from the upstream ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN and HyperMPNN releases. No raw human or web data is collected.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset contains no human data, no personally identifiable information and no annotator information; all sequences are computationally generated and all structures are public PDB entries.
rai:dataCollection: Backbone structures were downloaded from the RCSB PDB (public-domain experimental structures). Designed sequences were generated computationally by the 11 arms; refolded structures were predicted by ESMFold v1 and Protenix-2. No human subjects, no web scraping, no scraped personal data.
